title: Supabase Vector: The Postgres Vector database: Paul Copplestone
talk_summary: Paul Copplestone argues that Postgres + pgvector is a sufficient and often superior vector store for embeddings, using partitioning, triggers, and row-level security to handle messy data and multi-tenant access.

takeaways.technique: Partition embeddings by a cheap similarity predicate at insert time
takeaways.what_they_do: A Postgres trigger computes similarity of each new embedding against a canonical vector and routes the row into a 'good' or 'bad' partition; the good partition gets an index, the bad partition can be dropped wholesale.

takeaways.technique: Row-level security as defense in depth for per-agent/per-tenant data
takeaways.what_they_do: Declarative RLS rules on tables so that even if API-layer auth is bypassed, the database still restricts rows per user/tenant.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's also defense at depth so if it gets through maybe your API security you can go directly into uh your database the security is still there

takeaways.technique: Single round trip: keep embeddings next to operational data
takeaways.what_they_do: Store vectors in the same Postgres as operational rows so retrieval and metadata fetch are one query instead of two services.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you store your embeddings next to your operational data then you do a single fetch to your database
